item: row 409 stage 1: the split corpus's segment registry and id-range counter, with the crash rule
summary: Two additive tables in the shared file, corpus_segments (registry: number, file name, state reserved/open/closed/abandoned, id range) and corpus_id_counter, and src/database/segments.py. A segment comes to exist in three steps, each durable on its own: reserve (one shared-file transaction takes the range and moves the counter past it), the segment file's own transaction records its identity, then the row is marked open. reconcile() opens a reserved row only when its file records the exact number and range, else abandons it; the range stays used either way, so a crash may waste ids, never reuse them (R826 Q3, condition f; crash injected at three points in the tests). An empty or absent registry reads as legacy segment 0 and writes nothing; nothing in the app calls the writers yet, so an existing corpus is untouched (condition g). The registry is per machine: merge.py lists both tables as not carried. No behaviour change.
